name: Data centre UPS systems (double-conversion, lithium, modular)
aliases: uninterruptible power supply for data centres
principle: The UPS is the data centre's ride-through bridge: double-conversion units condition and back up the entire IT load, sized per hall and paralleled to hundreds of MW across a campus. The Vertiv Liebert EXL S1 spans 100-1200 kW per unit in the industry's smallest footprint and scales in parallel up to multi-MW systems; lithium-ion battery cabinets cut weight and footprint versus VRLA, and grid-interactive UPS fleets now also sell frequency response back to the grid (see idc-grid-interaction).

advantages: Ride-through of any mains disturbance for the full IT load
Lithium-ion cabinets cut footprint and weight versus VRLA
Parallel fleets can double as grid-frequency assets
limitations: Battery cycling for grid services trades backup margin against degradation
Conversion losses cost 2-4% of the load continuously in double-conversion mode
Large-unit lead times track the wider electrical-equipment backlog
